subject: Telemetry connector: fallbacks, rate-limit stitching, and pilot SOW
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@observix.io>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-09T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Observix -> Redwood: edge routing + fallback behavior (initial ask)

Hi Michael —

Thanks again for taking a look at Observix's telemetry connector. I've attached a short proposal that outlines our connector (edge OTLP relay) and the two integration patterns customers ask for: direct OTLP ingestion into Redwood, and agent-side forwarding into Datadog/Grafana. A few things we need to confirm from your side before we scope a pilot:

- Expected behavior when Redwood enforces per-tenant token rate limits: do you recommend retrying client-side (edge) or queuing at a server gateway?
- If we route to Datadog as a fallback how should we preserve trace-id continuity and sampling flags?
- Any constraints on header preservation (X-Request-Id, traceparent)?
- For the pilot, can Redwood provide dev credits or a sandbox endpoint to avoid production egress charges?

Attached: observix-integration-proposal.pdf (3 pages) — very high level.

Happy to jump on a technical sync next week if that helps. CCing Priya (partnerships) on timelines & procurement.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Integrations | Observix
samir@observix.io

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@observix.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-10T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observix -> Redwood: edge routing + fallback behavior (initial ask)

Hi Samir —

Thanks for the proposal, and welcome. High level answers first, then a suggested next step:

1) Rate limits / retries: we support three recommended patterns depending on customer needs —
   - Client-edge retry with exponential backoff (best for low-latency, best-effort telemetry)
   - Server-side gateway queue with bounded buffer and drop policy (predictable SLOs for high-volume tenants)
   - Continuous batching + KV-prefix cache for repeated keys (saves tokens for high-cardinality traces)

2) Fallback routing to Datadog/Grafana: we preserve trace-id and sampling headers by default as long as the connector forwards OTLP proto headers. If you translate to a vendor API, include traceparent and tracestate in the mapping.

3) Header preservation: Redwood's gateway can be configured to allowlist headers — we can permit X-Request-Id, traceparent, baggage keys, etc. Some headers we strip by default for PII reasons; we can document per-tenant allowlist rules.

Sandbox & credits: we can provision a sandbox endpoint and offer pilot credits (I will loop in Lauren for procurement).

Next step: technical sync Thursday 3/12 at 11:00 PT? Karthik is our integrations lead and will drive the API/compat checklist. Lauren will scope credits and SOW. I've also added a short shared doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-observix-integration-notes

Cheers,
Michael Grant
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-03-11T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observix -> Redwood: edge routing + fallback behavior (initial ask)

Thanks Samir — quick technical checklist before the sync. I'll paste the minimum items we'd like to validate in the proof-of-concept:

- Protocols: does your connector support OTLP over HTTP/GRPC and a JSON-over-HTTP fallback?
- Header mapping: can you forward the following raw headers untouched: traceparent, tracestate, X-Request-Id, X-Sampling-Priority? If not, we need explicit translation rules.
- Sampling controls: we support server-driven sampling via a token header (X-Redwood-Sample). Can you accept and honor that?
- Backpressure behavior: when client retries cause spikes, do you (A) drop oldest batches, (B) drop by tenant, or (C) throttle per connection? Please specify default and configurable options.
- Test endpoints: we have a sandbox ready: https://sandbox.redwood-inference.com/otlp/v1/push
  - Note: token=pilot-obsx-2027 is valid for 30 days for initial smoke tests.

If you can confirm the above, we'll prepare a minimal compatibility test harness (curl, small Python snippet) for Thursday's sync.

Hi Samir / Priya —

Great to meet you briefly on the thread. Quick procurement notes for the pilot:

- Pilot credits: Redwood can offer up to $10,000 in platform credits (applies to inference/ingestion egress units) for a 60-day pilot.
- Sandbox access: Michael and Karthik will provision a sandbox token (already done — see Karthik's token).
- SOW & MSA: we prefer a short SOW for the pilot with a brief attachment to the existing Redwood MSA. If you send a one-page SOW outlining success criteria (throughput, trace continuity, error-rate targets) we can fast-track signatures.
- Security questionnaire: if you have a short SOC or security questionnaire, please send it; otherwise we can provide our SOC 2 summary and data flow diagram.

I'll prepare a draft SOW template and share by EOD 3/12. Please confirm your procurement contact so we can loop them in.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop

From: Samir Patel <samir@observix.io>

Date: 2027-03-15T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Observix -> Redwood: edge routing + fallback behavior (pilot confirmation)

Thanks everyone — good plan. Quick confirmations from Observix:

- Protocol support: OTLP over GRPC + HTTP supported; we will add a JSON-over-HTTP toggle for legacy agents.
- Header preservation: we'll pass traceparent, tracestate, X-Request-Id as-is. We will accept X-Redwood-Sample if you set it at the gateway layer.
- Backpressure: default is per-connection throttling; we can branch per-tenant if needed (config flag).

Procurement: I attached a short SOW (observix-sow-v1.docx) that lists pilot success criteria: 10k events/min sustained for 2 hours, <0.5% dropped traces due to rate limiting, and trace-id continuity verified end-to-end. Observix procurement (procurement@observix.io) will review credits and sign the short SOW + Redwood MSA.

Next steps:
- Lauren: please send the SOW template and MSA excerpt; we'll return redlines within 48 hours.
- Karthik: we'll run the smoke tests against the sandbox token this week and share the results.
- Michael: thanks for the sandbox access — we'll aim to have an initial compatibility report by 2027-03-19.

Looking forward to the sync on Thursday 3/18 at 11:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Samir Patel
Head of Integrations | Observix
